issue_context.title: support `COALESCE PARTITION` for hash partitioned table
issue_context.body:
## Description

The 'ALTER TABLE ... COALESCE PARTITION' statement can adjust the partition count.

```
mysql> CREATE TABLE clients_lk (
    ->     id INT,
    ->     fname VARCHAR(30),
    ->     lname VARCHAR(30),
    ->     signed DATE
    -> )
    -> PARTITION BY LINEAR KEY(signed)
    -> PARTITIONS 12;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.03 sec)

mysql> ALTER TABLE clients_lk COALESCE PARTITION 4;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.06 sec)
Records: 0  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0
```

Consider https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/14999 and https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/15000 before taking this task, as `ALTER TABLE ... COALESCE PARTITION` is less frequent in practical use.

## Score

9885

## Mentor(s)

* @tiancaiamao 

Contact the mentors: **#tidb-challenge-program** channel in [TiDB Community](https://join.slack.com/t/tidbcommunity/shared_invite/enQtNzc0MzI4ODExMDc4LWYwYmIzMjZkYzJiNDUxMmZlN2FiMGJkZjAyMzQ5NGU0NGY0NzI3NTYwMjAyNGQ1N2I2ZjAxNzc1OGUwYWM0NzE)  Slack Workspace

## Recommended Skills

* Chinese: [TiDB 精选技术讲解文章](https://github.com/pingcap/presentations/blob/master/hackathon-2019/reference-document-of-hackathon-2019.md)

review_comments: Could you add a test case for `PartitionDefinitionClauseHistory`
The command is 'ADD PARTITION', so that is what I used here, but I don't mind changing the comment if you want?
I can't find the test case which produce this error. Could you add it?
Sure, let me either find or add it.

This would need to add another ADD/COALESCE PARTITION while there is already one running, so when they are picked up from the queue, the list of partition names does no-longer match.
Let me see if I can add a test for it.

I did not manage to create a test for it, but I did a manual test: first issue a `alter table t add partition partitions 1` when t contain some data and then when the alter started, concurrently issue a `alter table coalesce partition 1` it will hit this. Any other combination of add/coalesce it would fail earlier in checkReorgPartitionNames (since either it would reorganize/drop a no longer existing partition or add a partition with duplicate name).
So this line is all the real changes for this functionality ...
Correct, it is reusing the heavy lifting done and tested in Reorganize Partition (copy row data between partitions and recreating the indexes on each new partition).
The data of `table_rows` in `information_schema.partitions` is read from statistic, and it maybe inaccurate, we should use `select * from t partition (p1);` to check each partitions rows?
Should the data not be deterministic and at least aproximate? I can do a `SELECT` as well, but would like to keep the statistics there, to have it covered
It was probably before I fixed it [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/42476/files#diff-b162f5fd0f5d187791658b65d19334a3b8c3762542818bb1379f5163c65f5ed1R1429).
